newsitem.title: USA: UPS, union encouraged talks to end strike continue.
newsitem.headline: UPS, union encouraged talks to end strike continue.

text.p: Teamsters union President Ron Carey and United Parcel Service Chairman James Kelly Sunday both said they were encouraged that marathon talks to end the two-week-old strike crippling the nation's largest package carrier were continuing.

Neither official predicted how soon the talks would result in a contract that would end the strike by 185,000 drivers, loaders and sorters, but they said talks were continuing on a range of issues, including pensions and the number of part-time jobs. Both men were interviewed separately on NBC-TV's "Meet the Press" program.

"Obviously we're at the table. We are talking about the issues and that to me is progress -- trying to see if we can find some areas of agreement and the talks are moving along," Carey said, speaking about half an hour after the two sides resumed informal talks at a Washington hotel after a five-hour break.
Asked if the union planned to stay at the bargaining table until a deal was reached, Carey told NBC, "Absolutely." He said he did not believe a government-imposed cooling-off period was necessary.

Kelly said the two sides were continuing to discuss "dozens and dozens of issues" and it was unclear when an agreement could be reached. He said the strike was having a "devastating" impact on the company and the U.S. economy and said UPS still wanted President Clinton to intervene to end the strike.

"The fact that we're continuing to talk is encouraging," Kelly said, reiterating that the company would use replacement workers only as a last resort. Negotiators for the two sides continued meeting while the officials appeared on the television program, which was taped at 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT) in Washington for broadcast later Sunday.
